observations: The thinnest margin in the change is the body one character under the worker's threshold, which the page parses on its own thread: in Firefox the row '49 list markers on one line then blank lines' measured 844 ms in the full run and 701, 721, 721, 792, 874 ms over five more runs of that row alone, against the 1,000 ms bound, on an idle two-core pod. WebKit measures 443-556 ms and Chromium 330-344 ms for the same row. Nothing I could build at 4,000 characters costs more: 17 shapes measured in the read-only engine (100 quotes on one line then lazy lines 217 ms, a tab-indented list 49 deep 224 ms, 1,333 empty items 262 ms, a 400-row table 79 ms) are all under that row's 432 ms, so the suite already holds the worst case. It is the row most likely to flake on a loaded CI runner, and the lever if it does is the threshold, which is one constant (markdown-worker-threshold.ts).

At the cap, where a parse slower than the worker's 10 s deadline would be handed back to the page's own thread - the one way this design can still freeze a reader - the worst of 20 adversarial bodies measured in the read-only engine is 1,993 ms (a 4,000-row table) and 1,907 ms (a tab-indented list 49 deep then blank lines). Nothing comes near the deadline.

The two bails D1's label-end patch adds are the obvious way to bring the quadratic cost back, so I measured a bracket run beside the definitions that defeat each: a short link definition 173 ms, a footnote definition 152 ms, a 4,000-character link identifier 134 ms, a 10,000-character one 103 ms, 500 link definitions before the run 182 ms, a run of footnote calls with one definition 297 ms, against the unaccompanied run's 216 ms.
